B: Alright.
A: Erm, hi. Hi. Can you hear me okay?
B: Yeah, fine. Dean. Gillingham.
A: Kerry. Lowestoft.
B: Right.
A: Erm. Have you had your other calls already?
B: Yeah, two. One woman runs a shop in London, one does graphic design. Spent five minutes slagging off van wraps, so that was different.
A: Oh, was that Greta? I had her first. She told me about the Comic Sans on the funeral van.
B: Ha, yeah, same woman. She's alright actually. Bit sharp.
A: Yeah. I was a bit nervous of her at first but she was nice.
B: What do you do then?
A: Erm, nothing at the minute. I was a picker in a warehouse for six years, then they cut the shifts last spring. So I'm on Universal Credit, looking. Is that alright? I never know what to say for that question.
B: Course it is. Happens to loads of people. Our depot cut hours two years ago, that's why I'm part-time.
A: Oh, right. What depot?
B: Plumbing and heating supplies. I do the invoices and the phones. I had a forklift ticket once, it's lapsed now.
A: Oh, I've got mine. Forklift and pallet truck. I liked that bit actually, nobody bothers you. Headphones in, hit your pick rate, go home.
B: Yeah, that's the dream, mate. Nobody ringing you up asking where their copper pipe is.
A: That's why I don't want a phone job. I'd hate it. I'm applying for cleaning and that, early shifts. The hospital maybe.
B: Early shifts are alright. Done by two, whole afternoon.
A: Yeah. That's what I want. Just something steady, do you know what I mean. So I'm not worrying every time a bill comes.
B: Yeah. I get that. Skint all the time, me. Trying to save for a house with my girlfriend and it's just, er, not happening.
A: It's mad, isn't it. Everything's gone up. I go round Aldi and Iceland, I do a big batch of stuff and freeze it. Sausage casserole, pasta bake.
B: Pasta bake, yeah. That's our Monday, Tuesday and probably Wednesday. Jade does most of the cooking to be fair.
A: Is Jade your girlfriend?
B: Yeah. Seven years. Dental nurse.
A: Aw, that's nice. Seven years.
B: Yeah. People keep asking when we're getting married. Her mum mostly. She's round Sunday, so that'll come up.
A: Oh no. My mum used to do that when I was married, ask about babies. You just sort of smile, don't you.
B: Smile and pass the gravy. Yeah. That's it really.
A: Ha. Yeah.
B: You got the sea there then? Lowestoft.
A: Yeah, I walk the seafront most days, out to Pakefield. It's free and it sort of clears your head. Gets really windy though.
B: We go Margate sometimes. Camber Sands. Never go in the sea, it's freezing.
A: No, nobody goes in. You just get chips and sit in the car.
B: Ha, that's exactly what we do. Chips in the car, rain on the window.
A: Proper holiday.
B: Proper holiday. Did you want to ask me anything else, or
